nodes.summary: Let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be the Collatz map, which sends $n$ to $n / 2$ if $n$ is even and to $3n + 1$ if $n$ is odd. For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the $k$-th Collatz iterate of $n$ is $T^k(n)$, the result of applying $T$ to $n$ exactly $k$ times: $T^0(n) = n$ and $T^{k+1}(n) = T(T^k(n))$.
nodes.title: Iterates of the Collatz map

nodes.summary: The Collatz map $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ sends a natural number $n$ to $n / 2$ if $n$ is even and to $3n + 1$ if $n$ is odd.
nodes.title: The Collatz map

nodes.summary: Let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be the Collatz map, which sends $n$ to $n / 2$ if $n$ is even and to $3n + 1$ if $n$ is odd, and let $T^k$ denote its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n) = n$. For a natural number $n$, the Collatz stopping time of $n$ is undefined if $n = 0$ or if $T^k(n) \ne 1$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$; otherwise it is the least $k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $T^k(n) = 1$.
nodes.title: Collatz stopping time

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be the shortcut Collatz map on the natural numbers, $T(c) = c/2$ for even $c$ and $T(c) = (3c+1)/2$ for odd $c$, and let $m$ be a natural number with $m \le 91$. There are no natural numbers $n$ and $p > 0$ such that $T^i(n) > 2$ for all $i < p$, $T^p(n) = n$, $T^k(n) \ne n$ for all $k$ with $0 < k < p$, and exactly $m$ indices $i < p$ satisfy both $T^i(n) < T^{(i+1) \bmod p}(n)$ and…
nodes.title: No Collatz $m$-cycles with $m \le 91$ (Hercher)

nodes.summary: Let $A, B, U, V$ be power series in $\mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ with $A$, $B$ and $V$ odd (constant term $1$), let $T_{A,B}$ be the $q$-analog of the $3x+1$ map, and let $n \ge 0$ be an integer. Then there is an odd power series $W \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ with $T_{A,B}(U + q^{n+1} V) = T_{A,B}(U) + q^n W$.
nodes.title: A perturbation at $q^{n+1}$ moves to $q^n$ under $T_{A,B}$

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be odd power series in $\mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ (constant term $1$), let $T_{A,B}$ be the $q$-analog of the $3x+1$ map on $\mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, and let $T$ be the $3x+1$ map on the $2$-adic integers $\mathbb{Z}_2$. Then there is a bijection $h : \mathbb{Z}_2 \to \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ with $h^{-1}(T_{A,B}(h(x))) = T(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}_2$.
nodes.title: The $q$-Collatz map is conjugate to the $2$-adic $3x+1$ map

nodes.summary: Let $A, B \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ be odd (constant term $1$) and let $T_{A,B}$ be the $q$-analog of the $3x+1$ map. For every $x \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, $T_{A,B}(x) = x$ holds exactly when $x = 0$ or $x = B/(A+q)$. Moreover, for every $x \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, $T_{A,B}(T_{A,B}(x)) = x$ and $T_{A,B}(x) \ne x$ hold together exactly when $x = B/(A+q^2)$ or $x = qB/(A+q^2)$.
nodes.title: Fixed points and the $2$-cycle of the $q$-Collatz map

nodes.summary: Let $A, B, U, V$ be power series in $\mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ with $A$, $B$ and $V$ odd (constant term $1$), let $T_{A,B}$ be the $q$-analog of the $3x+1$ map, and let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $k \le n + 1$. Write $T_{A,B}^k$ for the $k$-th iterate of $T_{A,B}$. Then there is an odd power series $W \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ with $T_{A,B}^k(U + q^{n+1} V) = T_{A,B}^k(U) + q^{n+1-k} W$.
nodes.title: Iterates of $T_{A,B}$ move a perturbation at $q^{n+1}$ to $q^{n+1-k}$

nodes.summary: Let $A, B, U, V \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ with $A$, $B$ and $V$ odd (constant term $1$), let $T_{A,B}$ be the $q$-analog of the $3x+1$ map, and let $n \ge 0$ be an integer. Then the $n$-th iterates $T_{A,B}^n(U + q^n V)$ and $T_{A,B}^n(U)$ have different constant terms.
nodes.title: A perturbation at $q^n$ flips the parity of the $n$-th iterate

nodes.summary: Let $T_q = T_{1+q,1}$ be the $q$-analog of the $3x+1$ map with $A = 1 + q$ and $B = 1$, so that $T_q(x) = x/q$ if $q$ divides $x$ and $T_q(x) = ((1+q)x + 1)/q$ otherwise, and let $T$ be the $3x+1$ map on the $2$-adic integers $\mathbb{Z}_2$. Then there is a bijection $h : \mathbb{Z}_2 \to \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ with $h^{-1}(T_q(h(x))) = T(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}_2$.
nodes.title: The map $T_{1+q,1}$ is conjugate to the $2$-adic $3x+1$ map

nodes.summary: Let $T = T_{1,1+q^2}$ be the $q$-analog of the $3x+1$ map with $A = 1$ and $B = 1 + q^2$. For every polynomial $p$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$, some iterate $T^k(p)$ with $k \ge 0$ lies in $\{0, 1 + q, 1, q\}$, the set formed by the fixed points $0$ and $1 + q$ of $T$ and its $2$-cycle $\{1, q\}$. Moreover, for every $x \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, $T(x)$ is a polynomial if and only if $x$ is a polynomial.
nodes.title: Polynomial orbits of $T_{1,1+q^2}$

nodes.summary: Let $A, B \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ be odd (constant term $1$), let $\mathrm{PV}_{A,B}$ be the parity vector map of the $q$-analog $T_{A,B}$ of the $3x+1$ map, and let $n \ge 0$ be an integer. For all $a, b \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, we have $\mathrm{PV}_{A,B}(a) \equiv \mathrm{PV}_{A,B}(b) \pmod{2^{n+1}}$ in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ if and only if $q^{n+1}$ divides $a - b$.
nodes.title: Parity vectors detect congruence modulo $q^{n+1}$

nodes.summary: Let $A, B \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ be odd (constant term $1$), let $\mathrm{PV}_{A,B}$ be the parity vector map of the $q$-analog $T_{A,B}$ of the $3x+1$ map, and let $n \ge 1$ be an integer. Then there is a bijection $e : \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]/(q^n) \to \mathbb{Z}/2^n\mathbb{Z}$ such that, for every $a \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, $e$ sends the class of $a$ to the residue of $\mathrm{PV}_{A,B}(a)$ modulo $2^n$.
nodes.title: Parity vectors induce bijections modulo $q^n$

nodes.summary: For all $A, B \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, the parity vector of $0$ under the $q$-analog $T_{A,B}$ of the $3x+1$ map is $0$, that is, $\mathrm{PV}_{A,B}(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: The parity vector of $0$

nodes.summary: For power series $A, B, x \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, the parity vector of $x$ is the $2$-adic integer $\mathrm{PV}_{A,B}(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} x_k 2^k \in \mathbb{Z}_2$, where $x_k \in \{0, 1\}$ is the constant coefficient of the $k$-th iterate $T_{A,B}^k(x)$ of the $q$-analog $3x+1$ map $T_{A,B}$.
nodes.title: The parity vector of the q-analog 3x+1 map

nodes.summary: For all power series $A, B, y \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, the $q$-analog $3x+1$ map satisfies $T_{A,B}(qy) = y$.
nodes.title: The q-analog 3x+1 map on multiples of $q$

nodes.summary: For all power series $A, B \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, the $q$-analog $3x+1$ map satisfies $T_{A,B}(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Zero is a fixed point of the q-analog 3x+1 map

nodes.summary: For a power series $y = \sum_n y_n q^n \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, write $y/q$ for the power series $\sum_n y_{n+1} q^n$: the constant term of $y$ is discarded and the rest is divided by $q$. For power series $A, B \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, the map $T_{A,B} : \mathbb{F}_2[[q]] \to \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$ is defined by $T_{A,B}(x) = x/q$ if the constant term of $x$ is $0$, and $T_{A,B}(x) = (Ax + B)/q$ otherwise.
nodes.title: The q-analog of the 3x+1 map

nodes.summary: For every power series $y \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, applying the shift $\sum_n x_n q^n \mapsto \sum_n x_{n+1} q^n$ to $qy$ gives back $y$.
nodes.title: Dividing a multiple of $q$ by $q$

nodes.summary: For a power series $x = \sum_n x_n q^n \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$, its shift is the power series $\sum_n x_{n+1} q^n$, obtained by discarding the constant term of $x$ and dividing by $q$. In particular, the shift of $qy$ is $y$ for every $y \in \mathbb{F}_2[[q]]$.
nodes.title: Division by $q$ in $\mathbb{F}_2((q))$

nodes.summary: For every $2$-adic integer $x \in \mathbb{Z}_2$ whose residue modulo $2$ is nonzero, the residue of $3x + 1$ modulo $2$ is zero.
nodes.title: $3x + 1$ is even for odd $2$-adic $x$

nodes.summary: The $2$-adic $3x+1$ map $T : \mathbb{Z}_2 \to \mathbb{Z}_2$ satisfies $T(1) = 2$ and $T(2) = 1$.
nodes.title: The $2$-adic $3x+1$ map swaps $1$ and $2$

nodes.summary: The map $T : \mathbb{Z}_2 \to \mathbb{Z}_2$ is defined by $T(x) = x/2$ if $x$ is even and $T(x) = (3x+1)/2$ if $x$ is odd, where even and odd refer to the residue of $x$ modulo $2$.
nodes.title: The $2$-adic $3x+1$ map

nodes.summary: If the residue modulo $2$ of a $2$-adic integer $y \in \mathbb{Z}_2$ is zero, then $2$ divides $y$ in $\mathbb{Z}_2$.
nodes.title: Divisibility by $2$ from the residue modulo $2$

nodes.summary: Let $T : \mathbb{Z}_2 \to \mathbb{Z}_2$ be the $3x+1$ map on the $2$-adic integers. For every $x \in \mathbb{Z}_2$ whose residue modulo $2$ is zero, $2\,T(x) = x$.
nodes.title: Even branch of the $2$-adic $3x+1$ map

nodes.summary: Let $T : \mathbb{Z}_2 \to \mathbb{Z}_2$ be the $3x+1$ map on the $2$-adic integers. For every $x \in \mathbb{Z}_2$ whose residue modulo $2$ is nonzero, $2\,T(x) = 3x + 1$.
nodes.title: Odd branch of the $2$-adic $3x+1$ map

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
